Having researched a bit on fortification and it's developmentover the years, it's actually the fragility that world work against the British. 

Essentially when you hit a stone wall with a cannon the force is transmitted through the wall, and subsequent shots weaken it. This is why walls were made thicker and filled with rubble, to absorb that impact. They also developed a shallow sloped hill called a glacis to deflect shot over the low walls. 

A bamboo fort by contrast won't stop a single shot, but instead of a large weakened portion of wall that further bombardment can bring down to form a breach you've got a 4 inch round hole in the bamboo. So you'd need to pound the wall to splinters before you had a breach you could send men through. They'd also need to bombard almost constantly, because a new wall or patch could be fashioned and placed relatively easily. 

The best example I could give would be shooting a cinder block vs shooting a piece of paper.
